idiom_name: OrderMapper::save(const Order&) - delete/insert of std::vector<OrderLine> in one transaction
implementation_notes: C++ has no standard ORM, so the parent's mapper is an ordinary class: Order owns a std::vector<OrderLine> by value, and OrderMapper::save writes the order row and replaces the line rows inside a single database transaction; no OrderLineMapper or repository exists. The child's identity is positional - it has no id and nothing else references it - which is what makes the wholesale rewrite acceptable. The classic hand-written structure is the default in C++; only a code-generating ORM gives you the library form.
pitfalls: The transaction must own the whole delete/insert loop: a partially written line set is the failure mode, so the mapper must roll back on any error (RAII transaction object, or catch-and-rollback).

Holding the dependents by value in a std::vector invalidates references and iterators on reallocation and copies every element on copy - give the aggregate explicit ownership semantics before handing it around.

variants.name: ODB container of composite value types
variants.idiom_name: ODB #pragma db value + a container member of the parent
variants.implementation_notes: For projects already committed to ODB, the dependent is declared as a composite value type held in a container member of the parent object; the generated persistence code for the parent is the only path that reads and writes the dependent rows, and the value type has no object id and no independent persist/load/erase API of its own. Choose it when the child genuinely is part of the parent object and the team accepts the code generator and its schema; the hand-written mapper remains the better fit when the child table is hand-tuned or shared with other SQL.
pitfalls: Generated mapping code must be regenerated whenever the dependent type or its pragmas change; a stale generated file silently persists the old shape.
ODB's container semantics are its own: treat the value type as immutable-in-place where the manual requires it rather than assuming a mutable std::vector everywhere.
